title: Using a no-argument call when only a parameterized constructor exists
answer: If a class declares a parameterized constructor and does not declare a no-argument constructor, the compiler does not generate the default no-arg constructor. Therefore `new Type()` fails to compile unless an accessible no-arg constructor is explicitly available. Once any constructor is declared, developers must provide every additional constructor signature that callers or frameworks need.
